Old Aye Pensions

maintopic: SATURDAY SITTINGS
speechtext: I am referring to Friday, the 25th. A good many of us from the maritime provinces and the western provinces desire to have the opportunity of going home. I would point out the inequality of the position occupied by the members from the eastern section and the western section of the Dominion, as compared with the members from Ontario and Quebec. The latter are able to get home practically every week end; we are not. I spent six months and two days continuously here two years ago, and last year I was here for over four months. We do not have the opportunity of going home at all as have those of the central provinces. I would ask the Prime Minister that when we adjourn on the 24th, the house do not meet again until the following Monday.

maintopic: SATURDAY SITTINGS
speechtext: We need ten days to go home and get back again.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SATURDAY SITTINGS
speechtext: The government naturally is anxious to consult the convenience of the house generally, and I think the feeling of tfie house, taking it in a general way, is that it is now desirable to try and get through the session as speedily as possible. I believe that sitting on Saturdays will help to effect that result. I do not think it would be wise to adjourn over Friday and thus have three days on which we would not be sitting in that week when two of those three particular days might serve to conclude the business of the session.

maintopic: SATURDAY SITTINGS
speechtext: I will tell the Prime Minister that he will not get through on the Saturday.

maintopic: SATURDAY SITTINGS
speechtext:
I
would suggest that the Prime Minister do not press the motion to-day so that the members may have a little more time to consider the question of sitting on Saturday nights. I would remind the house of the situation that was created in former parliaments where the last few days of the session saw much important business rushed through without adequate consideration. If we sit on Saturday nights members will not have a minute's time to consider the questions before them. I suggest that we should have some time to consider them.

speechtext: On the orders of the day:

maintopic: OLD AGE PENSIONS
speechtext: I wish to direct the attention of the Minister of Labour to an article in the press which says, in connection with the old age pensions, that provincial appointments are in large measure under the control of the Minister of Labour and that the Minister of Labour would see to it that supporters of the Liberal party were placed in positions. Are such provincial appointments under his control or not?

maintopic: OLD AGE PENSIONS
speechtext: Would the hon. member tell me who made that statement and where he is reading from?

maintopic: OLD AGE PENSIONS
speechtext: I am reading from the Ottawa Journal of the ninth instant.

maintopic: OLD AGE PENSIONS
speechtext:
I assume the hon. member is reading from one of the local papers, quoting what a member of the Ontario legislature is reported as having said, namely, that the

Rabies in Ontario
reason he was against the old age pension plan was because the Minister of Labour had all the appointments under his authority. Conditions are just the reverse. Under this scheme the provincial government has full control over the administration and it makes all the appointments. DANGER TO BORDER RESIDENTS On the orders of the day:

speakeroldname: Right Hon. W. L. MACKENZIE KING (Prime Minister):

maintopic: CIVIL SERVICE
speechtext:
The hon. member for Toronto Northwest (Mr. Church) yesterday asked this question:

I desire to ask the Prime Minister (Mr. Mackenzie King) what will be done to protect Canadian citizens and Canadian interests at Port Colborne from the invasion of several armed American cruisers, as set out in articles in yesterday's Mail and Empire and the Toronto Star. One man was shot at. There is a heavy tourist traffic in this district at the opening of the season, and it is important that the necessary protective measures should be taken.
I asked to see the articles that I might give my hon. friend a reply to-day. Having seen them, I would say that the assumption that steps will be necessary to protect Canadian citizens and Canadian interests at Port Colborne from an invasion of several armed American cruisers is not borne out either by the newspaper articles to which the member for Toronto Northwest refers, or by other sources of infoimation. The shooting by coast-guards to which reference is made, was on the United States side of the border. speakeroldname: Right Hon. W. L. MACKENZIE KING (Prime Minister):
speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Order No. 5.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Resuming the adjourned debate on the motion of the Minister of Finance, that Mr. Speaker do now leave the chair for the house to go again into committee of supply, and on the proposed amendment thereto of Mr. Tolmie.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: The house should go into supply without question put on a Thursday, unless the rule is suspended. Otherwise I will leave the chair and no debate can go on.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: That is the only order on the paper relating to supply which can be called, Mr. Speaker.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Standing order 28 reads:
On Thursdays and Fridays %vben the order of the day is called for the house to go into committee of supply, or of ways and means, Mr. Speaker shall leave the chair without putting any question.
That is the case to-day. And if the house will bear with me, I will read also paragraph 233 of Beauchesne's Parliamentary Rules and Forms, which is a reproduction from May:
The adjournment of a debate on an amendment to the motion for the Speaker's leaving the chair-
We have the amendment of the hon. member for Victoria (Mr. Tolmie).
-may create an exceptional result, owing to the direction contained in standing order 28 that on Thursdays and Fridays when the order of the day is called for the bouse to go into committee of supply or of ways and means, Mr. Speaker shall leave the chair without putting any question, provided that, except with the consent of the house, the estimates of each department shall be first taken on a day other than Thursday or Friday. If an adjourned debate on such an amendment is standing upon the order paper when supply, for consideration of which in committee it is not necessary to propose the question for the Speaker's leaving the chair, is to be taken, the order of the day for resuming the adjourned debate is removed, and procedure on the amendment lapses, in order that the Speaker, in obedience to standing order 28 may leave the chair without question put.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Before you give your decision, Mr. Speaker, may I be allowed to say a word or two? I read over these clauses carefully this morning, and I submit that the action taken by the Prime Minister does not bring this clause into force. The Prime Minister called, "Order No. 5," and thereupon the assistant clerk read out:
Resuming the adjourned debate on the motion of the Minister of Finance, that Mr. Speaker do now leave the chair for the house to go again into committee of supply, and on the proposed amendment thereto of Mr. Tolmie.
As I understand it, it might have been possible for the Prime Minister, had he so chosen, to have called, "Supply", and thereupon Your Honour might have been able under this rule to leave the chair without question being put.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Which item would that
be on the order paper?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Simply "Supply"; no item at all. But the Prime Minister has called, "Order No. 5," and I thought that the Prime Minister had done this intentionally. If the Prime Minister wished to go on with the adjourned debate, which I think we ought to do at the very first opportunity, he could have taken no other action
than to call Order No. 5. According to the rule which Your Honour has cited, the Prime Minister could have taken advantage of it to go into supply without question being put. But he did not choose to take that position. Quite properly, I think, he called item No. 5, thereby implying that the government were willing to have this amendment disposed of. I submit for your consideration, Mr. Speaker, that by the mere calling of item No. 5 the government proposed to proceed with the discussion on the amendment in order that it might be disposed of and the business of the house expedited. Whether intentionally or not, the Prime Minister took the course necessary to resume the adjourned debate on the amendment, and, having done so, he must now go on with that adjourned debate as it was called by the Clerk Assistant.
Right Hon. W. L. MACKENZIE KING
(Prime Minister):	Mr. Speaker, my hon.
friend will recognize at once that the government cannot call an item which is not on the order paper. With respect to the item that was called, the government is restricted to those subjects that are on the order paper. Last night before the house adjourned it was announced that the government wished to proceed with supply to-day. The only number on the order paper which relates at all to supply is No. 5, and accordingly I moved that No. 5 be called. Whether as a consequence of going into supply to-day some amendment that is already before the house lapses, is entirely a matter governed by the rules, to which members of the government, like all other members, are subject. I believe it is a fact that the rules have been so drafted as to make it possible, notwithstanding what amendments there may be to the motion to go into supply, for the government to go into supply on Thursdays and Fridays. My hon. friend will see at once that unless there were some such rules a situation might be created whereby the government would never get into supply. But the rules provide that with respect to estimates that already have been under consideration on Thursdays and Fridays the government may get into supply by the Speaker leaving the chair without any question being put. Therefore the government is simply following the procedure applicable in such a case.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, I should like to endorse what has been said by the hon. member for Argenteuil. It seems to me that no motion to go intc
Supply-Procedure

supply, has of necessity to be made to-day under the rules, and that ordinarily, had it not been for the debate on the amendment to the motion to go into supply having been adjourned on Tuesday night, the Prime Minister would call what he wanted and that being supply you, sir, would automatically leave the chair and the committee would then be in supply. Being in supply, the Prime Minister would have the right to call for any departmental estimates he liked providing they had already been dealt with, and as far as I know the only two departments he could call would be Public Works and Agriculture, none other having been dealt with as yet. The Prime Minister called order No. 5, which is as follows-
Resuming the adjourned debate on the motion of the Minister of Finance, that Mr. Speaker do now leave the chair for the house to go again into committee of supply, and on the proposed amendment thereto of Mr. Tolmie.
-is it pretended that the debate which was carried on with you, sir, in the chair, could be carried on to-day with the house in committee? It seems to me that the proposition is preposterous. If the debate is to be resumed it can be resumed only in one way- with you in the chair. I am ready to concede at once that the Prime Minister can to-day, irrespective of the order mentioned, make a motion that we do proceed to supply, and thereupon another amendment could be moved. But the rules certainly provide that on Thursdays and Fridays you automatically leave the chair, and then the Prime Minister calls whatever is in order in committee of supply, and, as I have already said, the only two estimates open to him would be those of Public Works and Agriculture. I cannot see how it can be contended that the debate on the amendment is to be terminated by this procedure; or, on the other hand, that it could proceed in committee when it commenced in the house, where it must be concluded.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, the result which my
hon. friend claims would be preposterous has been foreseen not only in this house in the words which Your Honour has quoted from Beauchesne, but even in the British house.
I find at page 527 of May, 13th edition, the following:
The adjournment of the debate on an amendment proposed to the question for the Speaker's leaving the chair may create an exceptional result,

[Mr. Boys.)
It is exceptional.
-owing to the direction contained in standing order No. 17, that except on first going into committee of supply on the annual estimates or on a vote of credit, the Speaker shall leave the chair without putting any question. If an adjourned debate on that question is standing upon the notice paper when supply, for the consideration of which in committee it is not necessary to propose the question for the Speaker's leaving the chair, is to be taken, the order of the day for resuming the adjourned debate is removed, and procedure on the amendment lapses, in order that the Speaker, in obedience to the standing order, may leave the chair without question put.
As May says, it is an exceptional result, and it is the same as is worked out in this house by our rules, which provide that on Thursdays and Fridays the Speaker must leave the chair automatically when supply is to be taken. Of course, if it could be taken as my hon. friend from Argenteuil (Sir George Perley) suggests, merely by saying "supply" without reading the orders of the day, then this exceptional result would not happen either in the British house or here. But this is the first time I have heard it suggested that the house can take up any order of the day without specifying the number of it on the order paper.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, let us admit that the government had the right to call for supply on Thursday and Friday without the question being put. There were two courses open to the government in this instance. The Minister of Justice will not contend that the government had not the right to go on with the item on the order paper for resuming the adjourned debate on the motion and the amendment.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes; it would be against the letter and the spirit of standing order 28.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I beg my hon.
friend's pardon. He will not contend that the government had no power to propose going on with the item for resuming the adjourned debate. They had it in their power, according to his own argument. It was optional with them whether they would go on with the adjourned debate or would move the house into supply under the other rule, without question being put. I submit the Prime Minister has chosen the alternative of going on with this item. To argue otherwise, Mr. Speaker, reduces the procedure to an absurdity. How did the government lose the right of calling item No. 5 and proceeding with it? I submit, Mr. Speaker, that they had that power, and exercised it, and therefore they should go on with the adjourned debate.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, before the Conservative govern-

Supply-Procedure
ment came into power in 1911 a motion to go into supply could be made on every government day, and amendments disposed of and grievances remedied before the house went into supply. But after 1911, for the purpose of expediting the business of the house, the Borden administration had the rules changed so that on two days of the week, Thursdays and Fridays, the house would go automatically into supply without question put. The government has to abide by that rule; it is a standing order of the house. Unless therefore there is consent to waive the rule I do not see how the house can proceed with the motion and the amendment thereto, proposed by the hon. member for Victoria (Mr. Tolmie).

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: The Prime Minister called order No. 5. Will the hon. gentleman be good enough to read order No. 5.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: But the rule of the house lays it down that the Speaker shall leave the chair on Thursday and Friday without question put, unless the house consents to suspend that rule.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: My hon. friend's argument is that the government could call order No. 5-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: And did call it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
-or any other order.
Now what is the rule we are discussing? The rule in question is standing order 28, which provides:
On Thursdays and Fridays when the order of the day is called for the house to go into committee of supply or of ways and means, Mr. Speaker shall leave the chair without putting any question.
The rule does not say "may leave;" it says "shall leave the chair." It is imperative and no one has any discretion to alter the rule.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
That is the argument I am
making. The moment the Prime Minister calls supply, without any further discussion Mr. Speaker leaves the chair and the house goes into committee of supply. That is one procedure that could be followed. Another course the Prime Minister might adopt, if he saw fit, would be to call order No. 5, which of necessity would require the house to proceed with the debate begun the other day, and which would be a debate with Mr. Speaker in the chair, and not with the house in committee. That is the point we are contending for. If the other view is taken, what is the result? I do not suppose for a moment that this is a trick, nor do I think that the Prime Minister is trying to use it as a trick to avoid the motion and the amendment
thereto, moved by the hon. member for Victoria, being disposed of by the house. If however that course is persisted in it can be nothing but a trick; and judging from the way matters have been going in the last two or three days, my hon. friends should be the last to talk about free speech. There is not very much free speech; we are not given opportunities to move or to discuss amendments. And this is only a further effort along that line, if such is the intention. I cannot believe that this is the intention; I do not think the Prime Minister would want to bring about such a result. Let me read the rule in its entirety-because I cannot see anything in it which has the effect my hon. friends contend for:
On Thursdays and Fridays when the order of the day is called for the house to go into committee of supply or of ways and means, Mr. Speaker shall leave the chair without putting any question, provided that, except with the consent of the house, the estimates of each department shall be first taken on a day other than Thursday or Friday.
The Prime Minister had two courses open to him. He might have called supply, and rule 28 would have become effective. You, Mr. Speaker, would automatically have left the chair without any motion for the house to go into supply. The other course open to the Prime Minister was to do what as a matter of fact he did do-call order No. 5. That brings about a continuation of the debate upon the amendment which was moved the other night by the hon. member for Victoria. And surely, sir, that debate must continue with yourself in the chair; it must be resumed in the house, where it started. How could it be otherwise? Will anyone seriously contend that a debate, begun with the speaker in the chair, can by any rule be continued, and a vote taken upon the question at issue, with the house in committee? I think I am justified in describing such a proposition as preposterous.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: It happens in the British parliament.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I am not sufficiently well in-'
formed in that regard to say that it does not, but I can hardly imagine such a procedure being followed. Now is it necessary. If the desire of the government is to go into supply without continuing the debate already in progress, all they have to do is to call supply and under rule 28 Mr. Speaker leaves the chair, the only restriction being then that the committee may deal only with the estimates of the Department of Agriculture and Public Works. As a matter of fact I intended
2S74

asking the Prime Minister what the government had in mind if we did go into committee of supply. Will hon. gentlemen suggest that because of this situation they have a right to go into supply in connection with departments other than the two named?

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I am glad to hear that. I
have not much more to say. I appeal to the Prime Minister, in the absence of our leader (Mr. Bennett), to let the house go into supply without calling order No. 5. No one on this side of the house would, I think, object.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: But he has called order No. 5.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: My first duty is to see as far as may be possible that the rules of the house are observed. It is the duty of His Honour to decide what the rules are in the event of a difference of view. maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT

One more observation and I
am through. The Prime Minister called order No. 5, which is for the resumption of a debate which was adjourned with the Speaker in the chair. If that debate is continued it must continue with the Speaker n the chair, and standing order 28 is not in-roked in the circumstances. The calling of order No. 5 is not affected by standing order 28. Mr. Speaker was in the chair when the debate was adjourned and t'he debate must continue in the house and not in committee.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: May I ask you, Mr. Speaker, whether supply can be taken, as my hon. friend suggests, without order No. 5 being called?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: That is the government's business. If the government calls supply, either to-day or to-morrow, then automatically I leave the chair.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: But they did not say "supply".

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I have 'heard "supply"
called without reference to any order. The Minister of Finance says "supply".

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
But the clerk always
says "No. 5" or "No. 6".

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
