speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
My hon. friend says I called No. 5. But that is the only order on the paper that relates to the house
going into supply; it is the only order in order to get into supply that it is possible for the government to calk It is for His Honour to say whether, in accordance with the rules of the house, be can do otherwise than leave the chair and have the house go into supply.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: If the Prime Minister desired to go on with this adjourned debate to-day, what motion would he make?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
We should
have to suspend the rules of the house.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Not at all. One
word more. I do not want to inflict myself on the house, but I claim, as my hon. friend from North Simcoe (Mr. Boys) does, that standing order 28 has nothing at all to do with the question. I claim that the government, according to their own arguments,-supposing that they could call supply with this motion on the order paper-could, if they so wished, call supply and have the Speaker automatically leave the chair, under standing order 28. The government had a perfect right to go on with the adjourned debate if they saw fit, or they could -have had the Speaker leave the chair for the house to go into committee of supply without any motion being put.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Will my hon. friend allow me a question? Should his contention be right, and should we resume the adjourned debate, then the house would be called upon to discuss the question whether Mr. Speaker shall leave the chair, notwithstanding that the rule lays it down distinctly that on this very day, Thursday, he shall leave the chair without any motion being put. The house would therefore-if my hon. friend's contention is correct-be discussing a procedure which according to the standing order in question Mr. Speaker shall-not may-follow without any motion. My hon. friend from North Simcoe has advanced an argument which I would acknowledge had the Prime Minister said, for example, "No. 8" instead of No. 5. But the moment he called order No. 5 he called an order relating to supply; and under standing order 28. on Thursdays and Fridays, Mr. Speaker is bound to leave the chair without any question being put.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I would direct attention to the fact that there is before the house a

Supply-Procedure
motion of want of confidence, made so by the Prime Minister himself, and this government are not entitled to supply or anything else until this house has decided upon that motion.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: In our business to-day we have reached what are called the orders of the day; those are government orders. This program was prepared for the house by the government, and while the Prime Minister says he had to call order No. 5 because there was no other order he could call to get into supply, I would suggest that if there has been any neglect or oversight it has been on the part of the government in not preparing the order paper so that they could call an order that would get them into supply. The government prepared these orders; the Prime Minister has called order No. 5, so we cannot stop until we finish with that order. How can you call order No. 5 and stop short of everything included in that order?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: My hon. friend is mistaken when he says the government prepared the orders of the day; that is a part of the duties of the officers of the house, and the government has no control over it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Does the
Prime Minister seriously state that officials of this house go ahead and prepare anything that suits them?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I say it would be absolutely wrong for the government to insert any orders on the order paper other than those which come in the regular course of procedure, in accordance with the rules.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Then I
would say that the government have the responsibility of instructing their officials to prepare the order paper in such a way as will enable them to get on with their business. We have before us a program; order No. 5 has been called and that order must carry with it a continuance of the debate on the amendment. If that is not done I should like to know what becomes of this amendment.

speakeroldname: Mr. C. H. CAHAN (St. Lawrence-St. George):
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I submit for Your Honour's consideration that when the Prime Minister called order No. 5 he was entirely out of order, because by calling that order he insisted that we consider a formal motion that the Speaker do now leave the chair for the house to go into committee of supply, which carries with it a proposed amendment. The rules of the house provide that on Thursdays and Fridays Mr. Speaker shall leave the chair without
putting any question; therefore there is no question before the house. When supply is called no formal motion may be made and no formal question may be put to the house for decision; therefore I think the Prime Minister was out of order. It is only necessary now for the Speaker to decide that on this day, Thursday, we go into committee of supply without a formal motion. Nevertheless, the adjourned debate on another motion stands on the order paper, and at the proper time, on a Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday, the Speaker may be called upon to decide as to whether that motion and that amendment are still subsisting. They are not before the house to-day.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Would that not be a
question to discuss later, when the time comes?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Certainly, but the time is
not come. On this day there is no motion before the house, and there can be no decision by the Speaker on any motion to go into supply, because there is no motion. There can be no question put on this day, and therefore there is now nothing for the Speaker to decide, except that we now go into committee of supply by the Speaker leaving the chair, and on a future date His Honour may decide whether that formal motion No. 5 may take its regular place on the order paper.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: With all due respect to my hon. friend from St. Lawrence-St. George, I believe it is quite clear the government had open to them two courses: First, they might have determined to go into committee of supply automatically, in those departments which have had their estimates before the house previously. On the other hand, the government might have decided to move the house into supply of a department whose estimates have not been before us. I do not think there can be any dispute about that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: You cannot do it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
The Prime Minister or any member of the government to-day or tomorrow could move to go into supply of a department whose estimates have not been up already. That course was open to the government and the Prime Minister has made that motion. He has elected to move the house into supply, taking up a department which has not been in supply before, and in order to proceed with that business order No. 5 had to be called. To that order there is an amendment, and the Prime Minister has elected to continue the adjourned
Supply-Procedure

debate by Balling that particular order. Otherwise, what would be the result? This would provide a very convenient way for the Prime Minister and the government to avoid the discussion of a want of confidence motion; it would be simply necessary for the government to go on with government orders day by day and on Thursdays and Fridays go into committee of supply automatically, thus avoiding discussion of the want of confidence motion. Such a course would be preposterous, but that is exactly what the government propose to do to avoid continuing a very important debate which concerns the country at large.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
With all due reference to the Solicitor General, I think he was wrong in his presentation of the case. Standing order 17 provides:
Whenever government business has precedence, government orders may be called in such sequence as the government may think fit.
We have before us the government orders, and order No. 5 includes the adjourned debate. My friend the Solicitor General says it would be useless to proceed with that debate, because its termination may decide that the house should go into supply, which is absurd when the house does not need a motion to take up supply. That is an incidental result; it may happen that there may be a different ending to the discussion, but a motion having to do with the public business of the country is before the house as an amendment to the motion to take up supply and I submit that that should be discussed after having been called. If it should be an incidental result of that discussion that we decide to go into supply on a day when we do not need a motion to go into supply, I do not think that can make any possible difference to the precedence of that particular order of the day. I think this discussion should continue until the question is finally settled.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I would like to say just one word in reference to this particular motion. This amendment was moved on Tuesday evening; yesterday, being Wednesday, was a government day under the present rules, and the government proceeded with government orders. To-day, by the rules of the house, the government can go into supply automatically, but altogether apart from the question in dispute there is a question of policy involved, and when a similar question came up previously an illustrious predecessor of the present Prime Minister decided otherwise. In 1876 a question of this kind came before the house,

when Sir John A. Macdonald moved his famous national policy as an amendment to the motion to go into supply. The Right Hon. Alexander Mackenzie, who was then leading the government, said that it was a motion of want of confidence, just as the right hon. the Prime Minister has said; but in this' case he wanted that question resolved and determined by the house, and desired to take a private members' day in order to have it determined.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Is my hon. friend aware that the present rule governing Thursdays and Fridays was not in existence at that time?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I am not talking of the present rule; I am referring to the way the Right Hon. Alexander Mackenzie treated the question. In both cases there was a motion of want of confidence before the house. In one case the government wanted to have it determined, but in this case the government is trying to side-step the issue, and does not want a vote.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
The Speaker is the servant of the house and the slave of the rule. Standing order No. 28 is a new rule, dating from 1913, and reads as follows:
On Thursdays and Fridays when the order of the day is called for the house to go into committee of supply, or of ways and means, Mr. Speaker shall leave the chair without putting any question,

A situation arises to-day, here in the Canadian parliament, as has already arisen in the British parliament. Members need only refer to what May says at page 476 (12th edition) where exactly the same question arose. It so happens that by automatically leaving the chair to-day, as I am forced to do, the debate which was adjourned the other evening in good faith, on the motion which was presented by the hon. member for Victoria, would lapse. Certainly I cannot do otherwise but leave the chair-standing order No. 28 is imperative-but I do not rule that this debate, on a motion presented in good faith, shall thereby lapse. The procedure lapses, but the question can be revived. Here is what May says:
If an adjourned debate on such an amendment is standing upon the order paper when supply, for consideration of which in committee it is not necessary to propose the question for the Speaker's leaving the chair, is to be taken, the order of the day for resuming the adjourned debate is removed, and procedure on the amendment lapses, in order that the Speaker, ii\ obedience to standing order 28 may leave the chair without question put.
I must give a liberal and broad interpretation of this dictum of May's. The procedure may lapse, 'but the question itself is not

Supply-Public Works-Saskatchewan
lapsed, because there has been no judgment of the house on the question. It has simply been adjourned. When the time comes I will therefore allow that motion to be revived.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: By way of a new motion?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Certainly.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Can we be sure that the government will accept the ruling at that time?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: That will be a matter for the house. When I am in the chair on Mondays or Tuesdays, when supply is called, any member can move any grievance that he may have.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: If the government would accept it, I am quite sure their followers would. And if they would accept it there would be no question, and the debate would continue at a future time. I feel sure that no one on this side of the house wants anything more.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Will Your Honour
allow me to ask you one question? Does Your Honour rule that the government had no power to-day to call this order No. 5 in such a way that the adjourned debate on the motion to go into supply, and the proposed amendment thereto, might be proceeded with?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: By rule 28 I am forced automatically out of the chair. I must obey that rule. But, as I said a moment ago, on another day, when I am not automatically forced out the chair, a motion, similar to the one which was made the other evening, and which was adjourned by the hon. member for Halton (Mr. Anderson), can be made.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
In answer to
my hon. friend I would say that our desire is to follow the rules of the house, and, in every particular, the wishes of His Honour the Speaker. I do not think my hon. friend will find any difficulty in the question being revived at the right time.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I hope that is an assurance.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: It is.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: The amendment moved by my hon. friend, in the words of the right hon. Prime Minister, constitutes a motion of want of confidence. It is a desire to get from this house an expression of opinion as to whether or not this government has anjr right to get one dollar of supply. Now the proposition is that they be allowed to go ahead and get $100,000,000, or so, of supply, and later on, after they have got all the supply they want, the motion of want of confidence on going into supply may be brought in.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT

speechtext:
The 'house in committee of supply, Mr. Johnston in the chair.
Saskatoon-public building, $150,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I wish to get
some information from the minister regarding this item. We in Ontario are very much interested in the value of properties in Saskatoon. Years ago a number of our people bought lots out there, and I fancy that we could supply sites for post offices at very reasonable rates. I have no reason to doubt, if the information given to us is correct, that it is a very desirable location. I should like to ask the minister if the site for this building has been acquired?

speakeroldname: Hon. J. C. ELLIOTT (Minister of Public Works):
maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: The site has been acquired, subject, of course, to the passing of this estimate by this house. It is a site having a frontage of 150 feet on First avenue and 140 feet on Twenty-second street. It has been purchased from Butler Byers Brothers, Limited, for the sum of $53,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: From whom?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Butler Byers Brothers,
Limited. That is apparently a limited company.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Would the minister give us some further information? Could he give us tihe numbers of the lots?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I think it would be better if I just sent a plan over to my hon. friend. The present post office is in a building on the comer of First avenue and 21st street. That site is 83 feet by 71 feet and it is a very desirable site. The department endeavoured to get land in the immediate vicinity of it and they were offered two pieces but the cost of them would be about $102,500. As these two pieces of property had on them buildings which were leased, if we attempted to make a contract without expropriation, the best contract we could get was $102,500 for the additional land required and in addition we would have to bear whatever the cost of settling with the lessees would be. A site approximately 250 feet north on exactly the same street, on the comer of First avenue and 22nd street, was obtainable at $53,000 and that is the site which we have purchased. I will send across to my hon. friend a plan which has been prepared showing exactly the location of the site.
2878	COMMONS
Supply-Public Works-Saskatchewan

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Is the property that is being acquired vacant property.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Practically vacant.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Then we have
a property, 150 feet on one street by 140 feet on another, practically vacant, costing $53,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Can the minister give the committee any information as to the history of this property and the sales and purchases in connection with it shortly prior to its acquisition by the department; further, if any valuations had been made on behalf of the department before the agreement for the purchase was entered into?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I shall be glad to give
my hon. friend the information which he requires as far as we have it. This property was, according to our report, obtained by a company with a view to placing upon it a theatre or moving picture building. I cannot give my hon. friend the cost to them. It was obtained, I understand, in various pieces, but the report from our resident architect is that he considered $68,000, which was the amount first asked by the owners, a reasonable price for the site. We asked three men to value it. One realtor, Mr. Angus McMillan, was of the same opinion. Mr. J. H. Cameron, of Saskatoon, places the approximate value at $50,000, and Messrs. Heddle, Thorburn and Spring, at $48,950.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
What were the dates of
those valuations?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
They were immediately
prior to the order in council obtaining it and the order in council was passed on the 26th March.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I think the site secured for the new post office at Saskatoon is a very desirable location. While the price for the lot may seem high, it is not excessive according to values in that part of the city. I feel quite well pleased, and from all accounts I have received from Saskatoon I believe the people are well satisfied with the location for the new post office on the comer of 22nd street and First avenue.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
How long has
the department been considering the construction of a post office on this particular site, and how long before the date when the order in council was passed was it that the company acquired the property?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I cannot give the exact
dates in connection with either of the questions that my hon. friend has asked, but the question of extending accommodation for the post office, customs and various other Dominion services in Saskatoon dates back a number of years. The government have been considering for at least five or six vears the question of obtaining an additional site. The negotiations with regard to land in the immediate vicinity of the existing building have been going on for several years, but it was out of the question for the department to obtain that property at a price which they thought reasonable. The other land owned by the government was not considered at all suitable. If they could have secured for $53,000, or perhaps a larger amount, land in the immediate vicinity of the post office, they would have preferred that. But there were two objections to that. First of all our architect reported that the building did not lend itself to being transformed into a building giving additional accommodation for the services there. Of course, as my hon. friend knows, Saskatoon is a city that has grown very rapidly and in the last few years has been particularly active.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Did I understand the minister to say that he could or could not give the number of the lots? I understand there are three lots.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
The order in council
describes the property simply as property having a frontage of 150 feet on First avenue and a frontage of 140 feet on 22nd street.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
The minister must have
the lot numbers before him.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I do not have them here.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Could the minister say whether two of those lots had shortly before been sold by the city of Saskatoon for taxes?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I cannot say as to that; I have no information.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
The Daylight
Theatre Company who owned one of the lots recently, shortly before this purchase, apparently purchased it for a very small sum of money. Does the minister think he could obtain any information as to the earlier cost of these two lots?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I made very careful inquiries at the time, and my recollection is that while a small part of the property was

Supply-Public Works-Saskatchewan
purchased, probably at the tax sale to which ray hon. friend refers, at a smaller cost than the balance, yet my inquiries led me to believe that we were getting the property for very little more than it had been sold for. That is, some of the pieces had been purchased at a much higher price, but we were satisfied that the whole 150 feet was a valuable property and worth all that we were paying for it. We are also quite satisfied that it was wise to obtain it as we did, instead of taking expropriation proceedings.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
It is the first duty I presume of every hon. member to seek to express on the floor of this house the views and opinions of the constituency that he represents. To vote $150,000 for putting up a [public building in Saskatoon may or may not be a proper proceeding. I have a great admiration for Saskatoon, and such a building may be necessary, but when we vote $150,000 for this or any other purpose, by the passing of that vote we express our confidence in the judgment that the government will apply to the expenditure of this money. I believe I am expressing the views of the people of the county of Frontenac when I say that they have no confidence in the judgment of this government in connection with an expenditure of $150,000 or even $50, and there are reasons for that. We have only to walk a short distance down the street here to see whole city blocks that have been pulled down, costing millions of dollars, to satisfy the temporary whim of somebody or his idea of the 'beautification of Ottawa.
But there is another reason why I believe the people of my constituency, or a part of them, would ask me to oppose this vote at this time. People who are suffering the loss of much money every day because of unjust legislation, or because of the lack of proper legislation, have through their representatives in this house asked that that injustice be removed so that they shall no longer be subjected to this loss. The people of my constituency are working without any profit at all; they are working at a loss and suffering daily injustice 'because of the dumping of fruits and vegetables into this country, and they have asked this parliament to redress that grievance. We have taken the stand that that grievance should be redressed before any further money is put into the hands of this government to expend. Voicing the opinions of the people of my county, I say that we have no confidence in this government and in their judgment in spending this amount or any other amount, nor can we have any confidence in their sense of justice
and fair play, which is an indication of their lack of judgment so long as they refuse to rectify the wrongs and just grievances of our people before applying to parliament for the appropriation of further moneys. This simply drives home the fact that we are voting supply to a government to-day which has so manipulated things as to prevent this house from expressing its opinion as to whether they should be allowed to spend a five cent piece, let alone $150,000 or $1,000,000 or more. My judgment is that if the government had not prevented a discussion of the amendment, this house would have expressed such a vote upon it that my hon. friend the Minister of Public Works would have been relieved of the worry of getting through any estimates whatever.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Oh.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes, I have a right to suppose that a vote of want of confidence would have carried, and that the government would have been obliged to resign.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yesterday's vote did not look much like it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: My opinion is just as good as that of the hon. gentleman until the vote is taken. I have no doubt what the result would have been.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
On a point of order,
Mr. Chairman, I refer you to standing order 58, subsection (2), which reads:
Speeches in committee of the whole house must be strictly relevant to the item or clause under consideration.
I submit that the item under discussion is a vote of $150,000 for a post office at Saskatoon, and not the question which my hon. friend is discussing.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
But the money is to be
spent by the government.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I submit,
Mr. Chairman, that I have a perfect right to give reasons why this government should not be voted $150,000 or any other amount to spend in any part of Canada, and I am giving my reasons why. Like every other hon. gentleman in this house, I appreciate the fact that even to be recognized for a moment by one so great as the Minister of Railways and Canals is far better than not to be recognized at all.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Thank you.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
The hon. member knows the rule.
2880	COMMONS
Supply-Public Works-Saskatchewan

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes, perfectly.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
It says:
Speeches in committee of the whole house must be strictly relevant to the item or clause under consideration.
There is an old rule that the ruling of the chair cannot be criticized.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I am not
criticizing it. You have had a long experience in this house, Mr. Chairman, and I can assure you that it is hardly necessary to protect yourself ahead of time by suggesting that I might criticize your ruling.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I was
referring to the Speaker's ruling on the question of going into supply to-day.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I did not
know that I mentioned the Speaker. I was referring in general terms to the fact that the people in my constituency, whom I am here to represent, have no confidence in this government to spend this or any other amount, and surely when we are asked to express confidence in the government by voting this amount, we must be allowed to show why we have no confidence in them. However, I have covered that point as far as I wished to cover it.
I will now give another reason why I think this amount should not be placed in the hands of the minister to expend. Fourteen years ago a site was bought and paid for in the county of Frontenac, and no building has been erected on that site from that time to this. In the meantime, the people of my county have not got what you might call even half way decent accommodation at that place for the carrying on of the business of the country. I am perfectly safe in saying that the city of Saskatoon, having regard to its relative size and importance has far better accommodation, according to its population and needs, than has this little village in my constituency which has been entirely overlooked or disregarded. And for what reason? Because, we are repeatedly told, the government has not got the money to spend for this purpose. That is the reason we are given. Well, if the government has not money to spend to put up a five or six thousand dollar building to provide the people with the accommodation of which they are sorely in need, where is it going to get this hundred and fifty thousand dollars? I propose to take this stand, and I shall take it on other occasions, that in my judgment a government which has shown such an utter disregard of
[The Chairman.]
the needs of the people of Canada as this government has in throwing away millions of dollars to tear down city blocks in Ottawa for a park, part of which will be covered with concrete at a cost of 130,000, to be a monument for all time to the present Prime Minister-for I can conceive of no other reason why it is being done; beauty is out of the question altogether; the park cannot add one particle of beauty to these buildings-I say that a government which has shown such an utter disregard of the urgent requirements of the people from one end of Canada to the other by throwing away millions of dollars as it is doing to-day is not entitled to the confidence of the house in passing this or any other item.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I quite appreciate my
hon. friend's reference to the site in his own riding. His riding is in a similar position to many other ridings with regard to sites for public buildings purchased years ago and upon which, for various reasons, successive governments since that time 'have not seen their way clear to construct buildings. He also mentioned that in his opinion the town to which he refers was quite as much in need of a post office for the amount of public business it was doing as the city of Saskatoon. Now, I have no quarrel with him for expatiating on the merits of his town, but of course he knows that we in this house have heard of that centre before.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
And you
will hear of it again.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
We expect to hear of it
again; that is my hon. friend's privilege. No doubt it is deserving of all the commendation he has given it. But the circumstances in the city of Saskatoon are exceptional, and for the information of hon. members in every corner of the house I wish to give figures of the growth of business in that western city. The postmaster of Saskatoon states that twenty years ago the revenue of the post office was $19,711; while for the year ending March 31, 1927, it was $280,943.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
When was the present
post office built?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
In 1908. He says:
Therefore it is evident that since 1908, the time at which the present post office was built, the postal business in the city of Saskatoon has increased approximately 1,500 per cent.
I should be glad if every town in the Dominion was doing as well. I think my hon. friend will agree with me that under the

Supply-Public Works-Saskatchewan
present government, towards which he is not as enthusiastic as the great majority of the people are at the present time,-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: What majority?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
The majority you heard
about yesterday in this house.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
The government has been in
a minority for the last two years.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: My hon. friend may think so, but the votes do not show it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: The votes do show what was the popular opinion.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I am speaking of yesterday's vote in the house. I do not know whether my hon. friend was here or not. He is very sincere in thinking that he and his party got a majority of the votes yesterday, but he is mistaken; no doubt about that. I have looked over the record, and I was here when the division was taken.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I should like to put the minister right. He has a wrong impression of my thoughts. What I think and know is that of the popular vote taken at the last general election the Conservative party polled a decided majority.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
That is why we are
here.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: My hon. friend and I are agreed on one thing-that the vote taken at the last general election was a popular vote. But I was dealing with Saskatoon and the growth of its postal revenue in the last twenty years from $19,000 to $280,000. Of course, no one will contend that it is possible for the public business to be carried on properly in a building erected when Saskatoon was practically a city of tents. The customs and other branches of the public business have grown correspondingly.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Before the minister leaves the post office revenue,-of course, he is including in the figures the twelve sub post offices in the city.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes. I assume that there are newer post offices in that district. This, as everybody knows, is the main centre in that whole section.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Quite.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
My hon. friend is quite
right in saying that all the post offices for miles around will be served from Saskatoon.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: No, the minister misunderstands me. The revenue he gives is for the whole city of Saskatoon, including the various sub post offices there.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes. I always enjoy the suggestions of my hon. friend from Frontenac, for they are usually helpful. Of course, I cannot agree with them all, particularly when they apply to this government; but I do not know that any hon. member deserves more credit for presenting on every possible occasion the claims of one particular town in his riding. He does it well, but I am bound to tell him that the requirements at Saskatoon are much more urgent, and the accommodation much more inadequate, if I may say so, than possibly obtains at any other post office to-day. There is the same need for the other government services in the city, and it would not be in the interests of the exchequer not to provide this accommodation, because the revenue that this country needs, even under the most economical administration that it has ever had, cannot be efficiently collected unless reasonably suitable buildings are provided for the purpose.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, may I say with what unspeakable joy and felicity I listen to these delightful little tributes from the Minister of Public Works. Somehow or other they come to my ears more pleasantly than the commendations of the Minister of Railways and Canals (Mr. Dunning)-I suppose because the Minister of Public Works has cultivated a smile in connection with the discharge of his public duties, which is one of the finest assets that the King government possesses to-day. May I compliment him on the very skilful way he has of using the King's English, of selecting words with a desire to make you feel that you are bathing in taffy or molasses; while at the same time we know that he has not the slightest intention of granting any favours or fair play to anybody who sits on this side of the house. Nobody, unless he is a Grit and a good Grit, spelled with capital letters and rolled in sand to make it sufficiently gritty, will receive any sort of consideration from the Minister of Public Works. My hon. friend's supporters, whether they deserve it or not, will get the public buildings; we shall get the oily smiles. And that is all we shall get. But that is material of a kind that you cannot commercialize; you cannot make anything out of it in the way of selling it. It can be of use only here. I cannot get any money out of it to build a post office in Sydenham; I cannot get anything out of the minister's oily smiles. Now I do not want to be understood as opposing proper accommodation in the city of Saskatoon. I have had the privilege of visiting that city on many occasions, and in my humble judgment it is

2882	COMMONS
Supply-Public Works-Saskatchewan
one of the finest and most promising cities in the whole west. I am not opposing a vote of 8150,000 as being too much money to spend on the building of a post office there. I do not want to be understood as taking that position. I do not know whether it is too much or not. In all probability there is a lot of information, in regard to buildings that have been acquired and that sort of thing, which the minister has yet to supply us. I should be surprised if that were not the case. But he will open up after a while and be perfectly frank, and we shall know what all this property cost, what was paid, and who got the graft, if there was any, out there. But what I do emphasize is this. While the minister may be very properly spending this amount for this building in Saskatoon there are scores of places throughout the country that had to wait, and did wait patiently because of the war, and which are receiving no consideration whatever from this government, while at the same time the government can spend millions in tearing down buildings and in other useless work in the city of Ottawa. That is my point.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I do not intend to reply at further length to my hon. friend, except with regard to one statement. I refer to his request for an explanation as to who got the graft-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: If there was any.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Oh, I beg your pardon.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I put that in.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I want to assure my hon. friend absolutely that I shall be only too delighted to have the matter investigated as to the purchase of this building, the ownership of the land, and everything connected with it. I shall have it investigated to the very minutest detail, and I think my hon. friend will be satisfied that the best portion of his speech was that part in which he said, "if there was any."

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I am opposed to such a large expenditure on a public building in Saskatoon in view of the fact that, according to a return brought down to-day, one of the finest cities in western Ontario has been asking the Department of Public Works for the last twenty years, without success, for a new post office. I refer to the city of Windsor. The people there also made this request through the late Hon. W. C. Kennedy, one of the finest men who ever occupied a seat in this house -and this at a time when there were three cabinet ministers representing that part of

the country. In order to show the committee how this tally-ho is regarded by the public I may read an extract taken from the Border Cities Star under a full line heading: "New post office plans told by Odette. Ottawa ready to erect post office in Windsor now." Does the minister realize that when the old post office was built in 1879 Windsor had a population of only 6,000, whereas today, with the same post office standing, that population is 75,000. Let me inform the hon. gentleman that fun is being made in the city of Windsor, and some are becoming the butt of these good-natured jokes, because the hon. member for East Essex (Mr. Odette), is up against it. I quote from the Border Cities Star:
Local Boy Makes Good. A torchlight procession, hot-dog barbecue and bome-eomm' celebration is bein' organized in honour of Eddie Odette, who is expected to arrive in our midst soon with a new post office. Eddie recently visited the p.o. factory at Ottawa and looked over the new models, selecting a snappy four-door job, it is said, for this enterprisin' community.
I would suggest to the minister that it is time to quit this bally-hoo in connection with the Windsor post office and come across with a good appropriation, something definite in the estimates, for that city.
Mr. STEW'ART (Leeds):	The minister
was good enough to say that a proper investigation would be made with respect to this site.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: If it were wished.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I suggest that
the proper time to make an investigation is before the site is purchased. I am sure the minister must have made some investigation. He intimated that he had some information in regard to the amount of land sold recently for taxes. I desire to know more definitely how much of this site was sold for taxes. Can he tell us the total number of lots in the whole site, and by what material the valuator supported his conclusion as to the value of the property? It seems a very large sum for a piece of land 150 by 140 without buildings on it, except for some very inferior ones. Does the valuation show separately the value of the land and the value of the buildings?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I think I can satisfy my
hon. friend by quoting to him the prices asked for land

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I do not care
what was asked.

Supply-Public Works-Saskatchewan

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: -in the vicinity of the old post office, which is on the same street, 250 feet lower down.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: When it is found that the government wants to secure a site, the people desire to know a good deal more about the property than the information we have been given in this connection. It is the valuation I want.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I obtained the services of three reputable valuators, and I have given the valuations which they have made. Naturally they vary considerably, but I came to the conclusion that we were getting excellent value.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
There must be
some details in connection with these valuations, surely. They must intimate how many lots there are.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
No; we asked them to
value this piece of property 150 by 140 on that corner and they gave the valuations in lump sums.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Are we to understand that there are no details in regard to the valuations of the land and of the buildings-no details giving the number of the lots acquired? How many lots were there altogether?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
There are six lots, but I
do not see any details here. My recollection is that there were six.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: That would appear to be correct?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: That is what it would be on a 150-foot frontage.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: That would in' dicate that there were six lots?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: What is the city assessment of the property?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I have not the assessment.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Surely the valuator has given the minister something more than a brief statement as to what he considers this property to be worth. Surely he supports that statement by something in the nature of the assessment of the property, the values of the buildings, the values of sur-56103-183i
rounding property, and so on. Surely no valuator simply makes the bald statement, "I value this property, 150 by 140, at $52,000". or whatever the figure is. I should like to have the full details.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
That is what was done.
We sent out three valuators and they reported lump sums. We did not ask for details. We made the best deal we could and we think we have done well.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Surely in receiving these
valuations the minister would receive the numbers of the lots, the legal description of the property and the assessed value.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I knew that the legal
description of the property was 150 feet-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Surely the minister knows that is not a legal description of the property.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: It is quite legal, I may tell my hon. friend.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
It is quite legal. You
start at the corner and go down one street for 150 feet, then across parallel to the other street for 140 feet and so on. That is a perfectly legal description.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
The minister is a lawyer,
while I am not, but I will venture the statement that in any city, town or district where the property has been plotted and surveyed and where plans have been filed in the registry office, he will not describe any transfer of property by metes and bounds, nor will any other lawyer of reipute. Metes and bounds are used wherever the property is not surveyed or where a portion of a surveyed plot is described. I think there is no doubt that this property has been surveyed. Will the minister be good enough to tell me if this property coloured red on the plan and marked, "site of new building D on the corner of Twenty-second street and First avenue" includes lots 15, 16 and 17, and is the block number 148, plan Q2?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I am afraid I have not that information, although I think there would be no difficulty in getting it. I am satisfied that this property goes back 140 feet, with a frontage of 150 feet on First avenue.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Has the minister any
knowledge as to whether there are six lots or three lots in this property?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
The deputy advises me,
and this is my recollection of it, that there are six lots, but I am bound to tell my hon.
2884	COMMONS
Supply-Public Works-Saskatchewan
friend that the data before me does not show the number of lots. However, I do not think there is any doubt that these are 25 foot lots.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Has the minister the order in council concerning the purchase of these
lots?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: No, I simply have a memorandum that on March 25 an order in council was passed to purchase this property, but I will be glad to hand a copy of the order in council to my hon. friend.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Will the minister lay
that order in council on the table at six o'clock or eight o'clock.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes, as soon as I get it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Did the minister say this property was bought from Butler, Byers Brothers, Limited?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Who are these people?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: 1 could not say.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Does the minister know if they are dealers or real estate agents?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I could not say as to that; my information was that they were a company formed to build a theatre.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Did they own all this
property?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: The entire 150 feet?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: What have they been paid so far-just a deposit?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: They have not been paid anything.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
There was just an order
in council passed to purchase the property?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Did the minister consider expropriation?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Why was not that process followed?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I concluded that I had
to take the responsibility of getting this property for the best possible value, and I was quite satisfied that if it were expropriated it would cost the government more than $53,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
When did the minister
first open negotiations for the purchase of this property?
IMr, Elliott.]

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I would say in the early
part of March.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Has the minister the date of the valuations from which he quoted?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes. I do not have them here, but- I know they were made just prior to the passing of the order in council. The reason we proceeded as we did, I believe, was that plans had been drawn for the theatre, and unless we obtained the property at that time we would have had to pay more for it or would have had to get some other property one they started construction.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Could the minister tell us when instructions were given for making these valuations?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: That would be done shortly before the order in council was passed.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
There would
have to be a report before the passing of the order in council, and surely the minister can tell us when he gave instructions to have the valuations made?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: We had the general report on file in regard to this post office and the sites available; this has been a matter which has been very active in the department for years. There is a big file of correspondence in this connection, and I cannot think of any particular time within the last year or two when it became more active than at any other time until perhaps the latter part of February, or at any rate after the opening of the session.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: When the minister brings down the information at six o'clock could he inform the committee as to when instructions were first given to value this particular parcel of property?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes, I will be very glad to give that information. I know from personal knowledge that it was shortly before . this order in council was passed, because we were given the impression that we should act with some despatch if we desired to secure this piece of property.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I presume it
would be done by correspondence?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Might we have a copy of that correspondence?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I am not questioning the desirability of a post office in Saskatoon; like my hon. friend from Frontenac I know that city well and have known it for the last

Supply-Public Works-Saskatchewan
thirty years, ever since it was a small, insignificant place. Now it is one of the leading centres of the west, and must have adequate accommodation for its business. There can be no question of that, but these questions which we are asking are pertinent, and I am sure the minister has no objection to answering them.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I have not, and more than that I appreciate the interest of my hon. friends in asking them.

speechtext:

At present, the post office building, which is 83 by 71 feet, is situated on a lot 100 feet on First avenue by 90 feet on Twenty-first street, and was erected in 1907.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT

As the present site is now completely covered, if the building is to be increased, it will be necessary to purchase the property to the east on Twenty-first street, and to the north on First avenue. Should this additional property be acquired, it is considered advisable to increase the building in height, as well as in area, in order to accommodate all other government offices now in rented premises in Saskatoon. The present building, from a structural standpoint and the standpoint of appearance cannot be economically and satisfactorily enlarged in area and height. Accordingly, it has been found advisable to ascertain the cost of another suitable site, on which to erect a building of a size sufficient to accommodate the post office and all other departments of the Dominion service in Saskatoon. Mr. Stephenson, our district resident architect at Regina, was requested to report on various sites available, and on the 7th instant _ stated that to acquire additional property adjacent to the present site, the price asked for 50 feet on First avenue is $40,000; this has now been reduced to $37,500, and for 50 feet on Twenty-first street, $05,000; that in addition the government would have to take care of certain leases, which would be rather an expensive item. The total amount asked for land to increase the present site is $102,500, plus a further amount to take care of existing leases.
On the attached plan, the present site is marked "A". Mr. Stephenson further reports
that site "B", having a frontage of 150 feet on 21st street and 130 feet on 3rd avenue, belongs to various parties, and can be purchased for approximately $165,000, which he states he considers rather high. Site "C", having 130 feet on 3rd avenue and 150 feet on 22nd street, can be purchased for approximately $135,000. which Mr. Stephenson states is also rather high. Site "D", having 150 feet on First avenue and 140 feet on 22nd street, Mr. Stephenson reports can be purchased for approximately $68,000, and that this price is fair and reasonable.
This was the site that we got eventually for $53,000.
