Besides taking care of the postal business of the city, the office is a distributing centre for a large district and at the present time it is almost impossible for it to carry on business in a satisfactory way. I know the minister has heard this story a good many times in connection with other places, but it does seem to me that New Westminster should be attended to, particularly in view of the fact that the Post Office department, as I believe, has recommended that this addition is urgently and immediately required. The Postmaster General visited New Westminster himself not long ago, and if the Minister of Public Works would confer with him I am sure he would be told that this is really a case of urgent necessity.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: An application is on our list for an addition to the New Westminster building, the addition to cost $80,000. It is quite in line with a number of other places that have made a similar request.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I believe it has been recommended by the Post Office department to the Department of Public Works-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I 'have no doubt that is correct.
Mr. MoQUARRIE: -for immediate construction.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: A large number of places have been recommended for consideration. I agree with my hon. friends in regard to the traffic. Our records show that for the year ended July 31, 1927, something over 850.000 persons crossed the boundary at this point. That means between two and three thousand persons a day.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
In the course of time a
good deal of that traffic will go by the peace arch.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: There is a new road being built in that direction. The government has taken the right course in making these improvements, but it should not forget the other, because at present there is great inconvenience to tourists from California, Washington and Oregon, travelling north and south.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: There is a greater accommodation for the travelling public at this point.

Item agreed to.
Generally
Experimental farms - replacements, repairs, improvements, etc., $100,000; Flags for Dominion public buildings, $5,000; Installation of fuel saving devices, $10,000; Military buildings-repairs, fittings, alterations and additions, $50,000; Military hospitals-repairs and improvements, $79,000; Public buildings generally, $45,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
As there will not be another opportunity to refer to experimental farms I should like 1o again call the attention of the government to the importance of establishing an experimental farm in that great empire, northern British Columbia, a section of country very rich in natural resources, ideal for the production of live stock, excellent for dairying and good for all kinds of general farming. When I had the honour of occupying the position of Minister of Agriculture a favourable report was made by some of the experts of the department with regard to the necessity of placing an experimental farm in that section. With such a farm it would be possible to demonstrate quite clearly both to prospective settlers and to those already on the ground the opportunities of that great region, and in addition it would be a good point from which to carry on the distribution of live stock of improved quality. This is particularly necessary now because of the fact
Supply-Public Works

that the distribution of pure-bred sires, which was carried on for a number of years, has been suspended, and I sincerely hope the government will keep that section of the country in mind. I have travelled over a good part of it and can speak from experience. The prospects there are excellent indeed, and with a little encouragement and by opening up the country excellent results will be obtained.
Having brought this matter to the attention of the government, before taking my seat I would like to say one word about the prosperity of British Columbia in the line of mining, and to what that prosperity may be attributed. In the first place, we cannot mine without ore; certainly the ore was not placed in the ground by any Liberal government but by the Creator, and we who live in British Columbia are very thankful that it is there. For a long time a good deal of this ore, which was low grade, could not be mined successfully and put through the various processes of refining at a profit, but the oil flotation system was discovered only a few years ago and this put an end to that trouble. The big Sullivan mine, located in the Crowsnest region, was offered for sale to a prominent mining man in that country for $10,000 and he would not look at it. To-day that mine is turning out 4,000 tons of ore a day; it is being worked at a splendid profit and is one of the chief sources of supply for the smelters at Trail. That is also true of many other sections of the country; old mines which were abandoned years ago before the discovery of the present system of refining are now being opened up and are becoming quite prosperous. This prosperity extends over practically the entire province; it is not due to any Liberal administration but rather to the discovery of the ore and the methods through the use of which it is now possible to refine these ores at a profit.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Would the hon. member suggest that we cancel the bounty on copper rods?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I said all I wanted to say
when I was on my feet; I do not propose to receive any suggestions from my hon. friend.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I would like to direct just
one word to the Minister of Agriculture. The experimental farm for central and northern British Columbia which has been advocated by the hon. member for Victoria is really something which should appeal to the house at this time when the question of immigration is so much discussed and when solutions are being sought for the difficulties which have arisen in agriculture and dairying throughout Canada. Central and northern British Columbia,

as you all know, is an immense empire in itself, and never has had the privileges or the opportunities which other more fortunate parts of British Columbia have enjoyed in the matter of experimental farms. If the government really believe in the efficacy of experimental farms, which I believe they do, and knowing as they do the impetus given all branches of agriculture by the establishment of these farms, surely they should extend that system to northern and central British Columbia. The people of that great area have wonderful opportunities but they lack the scientific requirements which are essential in these modern days. I do not think anyone should have to direct the attention of the government to a matter of such importance. The Irish Free State

and I do not know why I bring this up, except that I read it lately- are adopting a splendid, up-to-date and progressive agricultural policy. Denmark is doing the same 'thing, realizing that the one way to keep their young men on the farms is to give 'them that scientific training and education in agricultural and dairying activities which is really essential. Therefore I trust that this government will seriously consider the advisability of adding to their existing experimental farms throughout Canada one more farm in this wonderful area, which will prove of great benefit in developing agricultural and dairying activities in a part of British Columbia admirably adapted for these industries.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Will the
Minister of Public Works explain the items of this expenditure? What is it all about?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: As my hon. friend can see from the estimates, a similar amount was voted last year. This is required for replacements, improvements, alterations, repairs and so on in connection with the several experimental farms and stations throughout the Dominion, requested by the Deputy Minister of the Department of Agriculture in a letter dated November 30, 1927.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:

speechtext:
The other night when these
estimates were under consideration I asked

Supply-Public Works
the minister if he could supply a list of the applications for public buildings throughout Canada, and he was kind enough to say that he could. To-night that list has been handed to me; I have it here, and I observe that the total number of buildings requested is 150, with a total estimated cost of $12,700,000. I understand that this list shows all the applications which have been under consideration, but which up to the present have not been granted by the department; they are still pending, but will not be granted this year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:

may be that some will be included in the supplementary estimates.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Then I will say that most of
them will not be granted this year, and at all events the supplementaries will show which of these items are taken care of.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Perhaps if my hon. friend would permit me, we might refer back to the item which was allowed to stand until this information was furnished.

speechtext: After we get through with this resolution?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Whatever meets the convenience of my hon. friend.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I would like to say what I have in mind first. I want to make some remarks with regard to this matter, but I am not in a position to do so to-night; I wish first to obtain some further information.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
My hon. friend may not
think that that list was prepared very hurriedly, but it was. In view of the returns in various branches which we have found it necessary to prepare, in the last couple of days, to say nothing of the preparation of the supplementary estimates, we perhaps have not been able to give it the necessary time. I have not looked over it very carefully myself, but that is tentatively a list that I would say is fairly accurate.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
You might put "E. & ,O.E."
on the bottom of it, and make it all right. I notice that there are some items which are not even carried out. I was not after an accurate list; I simply wanted a general statement which would give some indication of the situation. It is fairly long, and I am quite sure it would be interesting to many members in the house. I suppose it would take twenty or thirty minutes to read it, and if there is no objection I would ask that I might hand it in and let .it be printed. If we do that we save the time of the committee, and the information would then appear in Hansard.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
That is quite agreeable
to me, but I should like to have the opportunity of going over it again before it is printed. I thought my hon. friend would want to refer to it to-night while the estimates were under consideration. I should like to go over it with my hon. friend before that is done.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Perhaps at this juncture I
had better hand it back to the minister to give him an opportunity of checking it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
If the hon. member has
any remarks to make I should be glad to have them now.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I did not expect to get the
list to-night, and I have not the information that I would need to make the remarks. I would prefer to give it back, and have it checked over and corrected. Then, at a later date I can read it if necessary, or have it put on Hansard.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
My hon. friend can keep
it for his own purposes, and I will use the copy.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Let me clear up one question. I notice there is an item in this list for the city of Salmon Arm, covering a building for the forestry branch, Department of the Interior, S6,500. Do I understand from the minister that that is the only item there is for the city of Salmon Arm? I understand that there is a requisition in the department for a public building for general purposes. The idea I gathered in the city of Salmon Arm was that they were going to use the one building for postal, customs and fisheries purposes, as well as for the Department of the Interior.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I cannot give you the
details, but the amount of $6,500 cannot be intended to cover any other service of any great extent.

Your interpretation of it

Item agreed to.
Installation of fuel saving devices, $10,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: What type of fuel-saving devices are these, and where are they to be installed?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
It is what is called the
Burnhall fuel-saving device. It is a Canadian product, made in the town of Peterborough. I am advised by the officials of the department, who have made a study of it, that it has given good satisfaction, and has made a very substantial saving. I have a statement here which might be of interest to the house, made by, I think, a former member of this house for the county of Wentworth. This letter was written on March 10, 1924, and is in the way of a testimonial. It rather appealed to the department, because I see that they have it here in the data that has been supplied to me. It reads as follows:
I have your bill for the two Burnhall fuel savers, and enclose herewith cheque for the amount.
These have given us the utmost satisfaction. Our furnace man, who is a very reliable young man, assures us that there is a saving of approximately 25 per cent in the amount of coal used and we are satisfied that, with whatever amount of coal he uses, the house is kept at from three to five degrees warmer. He tells us that the thermometer on the furnace shows continually from ten to fifteen degrees greater heat in the water.
I note that you guarantee this device for ten years, and that it will never be too much trouble for your engineer to call and explain anything, or to fix anything that might by any chance go wrong, which seems impossible, as the device is very simple.
That letter was signed by Mr. E. D. Smith, of Winona. I think it is a good device and a good investment.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Will the minister tell
us what kind of fuel this device bums?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Soft coal screenings?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
At what points are you
going to install it?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT

I could give you, in a
general way, the buildings in which we have installed it for a number of years. In 1922-23 we installed it at Barrie, Belleville, Brockville, Cobourg, Guelph, Lakefield, Lindsay, Milverton, Newmarket, and several other places. In
1923-	24 we installed it at Montreal, a number of buildings in Ottawa, Aylmer, Amherstburg, Aurora, Bracebridge, Bowmanville, Carleton Place, Chatham, Deseronto, and so on. In
1924-	25, at Hull, Ottawa experimental farm, in a number of buildings, St. Catharines, Niagara Falls, Bridgeburg, Dundas, Paris, Burford, Simcoe, Elmira, Elora, and so on.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I understand from the
minister that it is purely a device for heating buildings?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:

Canadian invention?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Has the minister made any experiments in connection with smokeconsuming devices? This city of Ottawa is a very dirty city so far as the atmosphere is concerned, and it would seem advisable, when we are talking about the beautification of the city, that the government, with all the buildings that it has here, should endeavour to do something in the way of taking care of the smoke from the various chimneys. Is anything being done along that line?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: We have what are known as automatic stokers in a number of our largest buildings. They are smoke consumers, more or less; that is, they eliminate a good deal of the smoke.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I may be able to offer to the Minister of Public Works a suggestion that will enable him to get rid of the smoke nuisance of which my hon. friend speaks. If the government would take advantage of the excellent rate on coal from Alberta to Ottawa and use that coal in their public buildings, they would have very little, if any, smoke or soot. They would also be doing a very patriotic act in that they would be helping to get a market for Alberta coal definitely established, at least in Ottawa.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I can give the minister
a very much better suggestion, namely, that he should use Nova Scotia coke and then he would have no smoke at all.

Supply-Public Works

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I know my hon. friend
will be glad to hear that we are using it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I hope the minister will extend the use of it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
What is the cost of
these fuel savers?
Mr, ELLIOTT:	They vary according to
the size of the building. The prices generally are as follows:
Barrie	 $342
Belleville	 346
Brockville	 489
Lindsay	 575
Milverton	 375

Public buildings generally, $45,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Before six o'clock I was
promised an opportunity under this item of bringing before the minister the question of the urgency of a public building in the town of Biggar. I was assured last year that it would have very sympathetic consideration and the Postmaster General went so far as to get a report. I was in hopes that this year, owing to the urgency of the case, an item for the erection of this building would be included in the estimates. A post office official in Saskatoon assured me that there was no other place he knew of where there was such urgency as in Biggar for the erection of a public building. Biggar is a growing town with a population now of nearly 3,000, and it is almost impossible to rent a suitable building. It is a railway centre with the two main lines of the Canadian Pacific and the Canadian National and also lines running north and south. It is a divisional point and the railways have established repair shops there. Comparing the revenue from this office with the revenues of other places where the government have considered it necessary to make appropriations for the erection of public buildings, I find the figures are as follows: Town	Revenue
Tisdale	 $6,957
Durham	 5,683
Rockland	 2,412
Wainwright	 5,957
The post office alone at Biggar has a revenue of nearly $9,000. This shows the importance of the place. It commands a wide district.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: What has been the increase in population, say in the last ten years, or has there been any?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I do not know what the increase has been, but the population at present is upwards of 2,800. I want to impress upon the minister who, I believe, knows something of the district himself-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I know it well.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
-that it is impossible to
rent a suitable building. There is not room even for the boxes that are needed and the fire hazard is tremendous. I hope the government will see fit to increase the supplementary estimates sufficiently to include an item for a public building in Biggar because it is an urgent case.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
The other day when the
minister was putting through his items for New Brunswick a considerable discussion took place and the matter was left over. He said that we could discuss public buildings generally when this item came up. You can talk all day about public buildings in the- west, in Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Alberta, British Columbia

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
May I interrupt my hon.
friend for a moment? He is referring to St. Stephen?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Yes, but the minister said
that when this item came up we could discuss public buildings generally; that we could take in the whole country.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT

Unfortunately my hon.
friends did not accept the suggestion and the item was left over. I suggest that we revert to it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: The minister will not revert to the New Brunswick item to-night because there are not many members from that province present.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Perhaps my hon. friend
will defer his discussion.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
The other day the minister
stated that when this item came up we could discuss public buildings generally. The minister has made appropriations very generously for the west and I want to call his attention to the fact that in Nova Scotia, outside of the city of Halifax, only $14,500 is appropriated for public buildings. Does he think that is a fair proportion to be allotted for public buildings in Nova Scotia? Why is it that Ontario, Quebec and particularly Saskatchewan have been so liberally looked after in the way of public buildings and Nova Scotia completely neglected? A public
Supply-Public Works

building is urgently required in Bridgetown in the constituency which I have the honour to represent. This matter was brought to the minister's attention last year; in fact, it has been brought to his attention since 1925. They evidently thought the matter was urgent then because a site was purchased for that building. The Liberal candidate in 1925 and 1926 promised that if he was elected a public building would be erected there. I want to know what the policy of the government is? Are they going to erect buildings only in those constituencies that are represented by their Liberal friends?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Is that the policy-to the
victor belong the spoils? I want to tell my hon. friend that that day has gone by. People are not living in the past. We on this side of the house are just as much entitled to appropriations as my hon. friends opposite are and we are going to get them; otherwise we are going to hold up some of these other items or at least criticize them. I should like to know what the disposition of the minister is with respect to the Bridgetown post office. The minister's predecessor, the present Minister of Health (Mr. King), when Minister of Public Works, made the statement when his estimates were before the committee that he had visited Bridgetown and that the post office there was a perfect disgrace, and so it is. The postal revenue i3 $6,600, and the customs revenue $10,800. We have not a public building of any kind. It is nothing but a shack, practically, that the post office is in; it is a disgrace to the community. The government is making liberal appropriations for other parts of the country, and I do hope that the minister will consider the application from Bridgetown and that an item will be placed in the supplementary estimates to provide for a public building there.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I see it is in the list that we have, a public building at an estimated cost of $36,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Will an item for that amount be included in the supplementaries?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I would have to consult
the treasury board and council.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Has the minister in that list an application for a post office in Oxford, in the county of Cumberland, Nova Scotia?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: That is good enough if you will give us the building.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Has the minister received
representations from the town of Biggar? I think he is impressed with the urgency of the case, and I should like to know if an item will be included in the supplementary estimates.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I see that a public building for Biggar is included in the list, at an estimated cost of $30,000. I have spent a good deal of time in that district and know the town of Biggar well. I do not think it is one' of those towns that are growing rapidly, but as I recollect the figures it has a fairly healthy growth. Some time ago I went over some of the requests that had been made. I think the board of trade has sent in a request with regard to Biggar within the last six months, and I can assure my hon. friend that it will not be forgotten.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I understand that the list which the minister has compiled contains about 150 applications.
M'r. ELLIOTT: To be accurate, 154.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
And that the total cost is $12,700,000. I suggest to the minister, in view of the spending government that we have and the generous treatment that is being accorded to Ottawa

I see items here for Ottawa totalling about $8,000',000-the minister might well appropriate S12,700,000 for public buildings that are urgently needed for these 154 places all over the country, and then everybody would be happy.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Of course there are a lot more than 150 places in the Dominion.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Well, then next year you would have another list of 150.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: That is just the point I was going to make.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Is Camrose on that list?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: What is the estimated cost?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: That is in cold storage.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: It is a cold locality.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: No, quite the contrary. The very name indicates that it is the rose garden of the west.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Has the minister the town of New Waterford on that list?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Yes, there is no doubt
about that.

Supply-Public Works

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Did the minister say he was going to do something for New Waterford? Last year two delegations came up here from that town, and they had the assistance of the hon. member for Antigonish-Guysborough. New Waterford is an incorporated town of from eight to ten thousand people, with a town council and board of trade, and all civic improvements, such as sidewalks, sewers and so forth, and five or six large schools. The post office is only about twelve by twenty, and it is not even on the front street, but is in the back part of the building and is entirely too small for the business that is done there. There is a postal revenue of about $6,000 and a customs revenue of about the same amount. Urgent representatipns have been made to the minister in this regard, and I would ask if there is any possibility of the government considering the application favourably and of an item being included in the supplementary estimates.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I would not hold out a great deal of hope to my hon. friend for an item in the Supplementary estimates. So far as my information goes, I cannot see that New Waterford is in any more fortunate position than a great many other places on this list, and from what I know of the gentlemen that I have to get past with the supplementary estimates, I would not think that there will be a large list.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: With all deference to the minister, I think the house should be given some idea of the system upon which these grants are made. Last year we had a vote of $16,000 for a post office at Kensington, and this year there have been three or four votes of from $20,000 to $30,000 for small towns in the province of Quebec that are perhaps only one-fifth the size of New Waterford. There must be some method by which the minister can be approached, and I was wondering whether it was the physical size of the members who represent these constituencies. I see that my hon. friend from Melfort got a vote through, also the hon. member for Princeton, who is a very large man. Are physical threats necessary to get a vote?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: If size or good looks have anything to do with it, my hon. friend will stand an excellent chance.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: That is very pleasant indeed, but I would rather take home some assurance that the minister will consider favourably the application of New Waterford.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: What are the details of the $45,000?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: This' vote is required for items of expenditure which have to be met every year in connection with public buildings controlled by the Dominion government, together with such special outlays for works as cannot be charged against any other of the general appropriations made by parliament for prospective improvements in the several provinces.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I would like to refer again to the question of public buildings in Nova Scotia. The hon. member for Digfoy-An-napolis in referring to the vote for Nova Scotia was over generous. The total amount for Nova Scotia, as given on page 31 of the estimates, outside of the government buildings in Halifax, is $7,500. In the list which the minister was good enough to give to my hon. friend, the total number of buildings is ten, and the total estimated cost, $127,000- a mere bagatelle as compared with votes for public buildings in many other sections of the country. To refresh the minister's memory in regard to the alterations and repairs to the public building in New Glasgow, let me say that we have a postal revenue of practically $3,000 a month or $36,000 a year. We have customs and excise of about a quarter of a million dollars a year. That building is certainly nearly fifty years old. The minister is thoroughly familiar with the whole situation. Will he be good enough to tell me what he is going to do about it?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Nothing has been decided for this year.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: That is not very satisfactory. We went over this whole question last year. I think the minister made me a promise with regard to it at that time. Is he disposed to fulfil his undertaking?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I will certainly fulfil anything I said to my hon. friend or to anybody else. But I am not going to put myself in the position-of having him come back and say that I made him a promise and did not keep it. He got pretty close to that last year-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Yes, he did.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: -and is just bordering on it again. I am as near it as I intend to be at the present time.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Instead of just bordering on it again the minister is sliding away from it again.

Supply

Public Works

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: No, I am quite as near it as I ever was with my hon. friend.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: He is flirting with it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: No, I never do that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Possibly the minister
might be better off if he had done a little flirting and then decided on the date. But I should like to get an assurance that he is going to make the alterations in that building that he knows, that ihis deputy knows, and that the postal department knows are absolutely necessary and have been for some years. I am quite sure he will admit that he has in his department letters from the postal department calling attention to the conditions and stating that they are disgraceful, and that in the public interest the building ought to be remodelled. A year ago the plans for the alterations and addition to the building were revised and the cost very materially reduced, and I understood from him last session that this year the matter would be attended to. Now I ask him to carry out what I understood to be a virtual promise in that connection. I want some assurance.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I know my hon. friend is quite sincere when he says he wants some assurance.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
"Sincere" does not
measure up the situation at all. I am in earnest, I want it, and I expect him to give it to me.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I quite admit he has been in earnest; hle has been any time he spoke to me about it. And the other 1491 gentlemen who have asked for the balance of this list are also in earnest. There is no doubt about their sincerity or mine, but what will be done this year or next year is more than I can promise, because if I promise my hon. friend definitely-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Your troubles would end right away.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: They would! My good friend from Rosetown (Mr. Evans) would think that he was entitled to a promise, and he would be if my hon. friend in this quarter was, and knowing something of human nature I have not any doubt that every hon. gentleman representing a riding mentioned in this list-which I was unfortunate enough to give to my genial friend from North Simcoe- would want similar assurances.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I am very sorry the minister makes any reflection on my sincerity or his own.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Will my hon. friend permit me? I disclaim making any reflection whatever on my hon. friend's sincerity in any respect, and especially in respect to this particular public building. No man ever was more sincere.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Thank you.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: There is no doubt about that. Perhaps my hon. friend from Skeena (Mr. Brady) is in the same class. But I have no doubt about the sincerity of any hon. gentlemen who have asked for buildings, and I hope they will give me credit for equal sincerity in connection with the matter.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Mr. Chairman, I am not asking for a building. All I am asking for is to have a patch put on a building. The matter of sincerity was raised by the minister. He disclaims referring to my sincerity. I hope he did not refer to his own.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
I
wish to call the attention of the minister to the flag over the post office at Harriston, my home town. The last time I was home it was at half mast and all in ribbons. I now ask him to send along a flag for the building. This is the first time this session that I have asked him for anything.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Send the flag along.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: While we are on this item I wish to refer to one or two matters in connection with these votes, some of which have been passed. In considering the generosity, I might say the enormity of many of the votes which have been passed, I think we in the eastern end of the Dominion must conolude that we are getting really the pin point, not the pinhead. In anything I say I do not wish to create a feeling of jealousy between provinces and districts, but let me call the attention of the committee to the fact that during the last two or three days I find with respect to Ottawa that instead of nearly five million dollars having been voted, as was stated a few days ago, the total is ten million dollars, and this does not include several small items which might reasonably come under that head. I take vote 127, and there I find for Ottawa a total of $3,220,000 odd.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
My hon. friend will find that vote 127 in the aggregate is only $1,200,-940-a great difference.

Supply-Public Works

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: I should have said $382,000. Then I take vote 132, and I estimate the proportion of that applicable to Ottawa is $96,000-a third of the whole.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: It is only $38,000.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Very well, we will cut that down, but I do not know how you arrive at your figure. I take it that the experimental farm-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
That is the part of the
experimental farm vote that will foe spent in Ottawa.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Where is the $60,000 being spent?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: On branch farms outside of Ottawa.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Then I go on to 133 and I find in the first dozen items, down to and including telephone service, the sum of $1,854,500 expended in Ottawa. That does not include rentals, which total $1,565,000, over $700,000 of which is spent in Ottawa. I am not estimating at all the salaries of caretakers and all that sort of thing. With the exception of the last two, a certain proportion of all these items must be fairly chargeable to the vote for Ottawa, but I am not including any of them. Then I come to another item, 121, $1,380,000 for Ottawa alone. Item 145 is a small item, it is true, $14,600; and as regards item 144, there is a dredge at work in the canal digging out what was put in in the winter time.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: That is not under public works.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
In item 150 we find, for the National Gallery of Canada, $135,000, and for the national monument on Connaught place $35,000. During the hot weather in the summer it will be pretty nice walking around on the hot tar looking at that monument, instead of walking on a green plot, won't it? Then we come to the $3,000,000 to the federal improvement commission; and there is $200,000 annually to that organization. For the New Edinburgh mills there is the sum of $525,000 and $100,000 for repairs. Under item 232, observatories at Ottawa, we have an expenditure of $75,000 as against $59,000 last year. So that adding all these figures together, you have practically $9,000,000. That does not include any expenditure in connection with the Rideau canal; I could not locate what had been allocated to that. I understand, further, that there is an expenditure of $4,000,000 in con-56103-1851
nection with the Chateau Laurier. That means, over $13,000,000 spent in Ottawa by this government. But what do we find in regard to Nova Scotia? In the estimates little Nova Scotia gets, for buildings, $84,500, while you are expending'$13,000,000 in Ottawa. What justice is there in such a condition of things as that? What justification is there for it? I will not refer to national parks. Suffice it to say that out of $1,300,000 odd in the estimates for national parks we had an expenditure last year or the year before in What might be called a national park, inasmuch as it is owned by the Dominion, of $1,800, and a small expenditure in Annapolis for a fortification. That perhaps does not come under this vote. But this is the way that we in the east have been treated, not only by this government but by previous governments as well. When we apply for a small grant it is not given us.
I must protest most vigorously against the neglect shown the maritime provinces and particularly Nova Scotia in relation to these votes from year to year. We are contributing our full quota and we are not getting half of what we pay. I may be told by some hon. gentlemen, "Look at your breakwaters, wharves and so on". But my reply would be: Are there none in Quebec and Ontario and in the Pacific province of British Columbia and elsewhere throughout the Dominion? Look at the estimates and you will find $2,000,000 for breakwaters in Quebec, while we in Nova Scotia receive less than $500,000, a quarter of what they get in Quebec. I could spend an hour referring to these discrepancies which appear in this blue book, the official publication of the government, but I have said enough to call the attention of the government to the injustice and I hope that some consideration will be given us in Nova Scotia, if not in the supplementary estimates then in another year.
Item agreed to.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: We have only a minute or two left but perhaps we might consider Saskatoon, in regard to which I gave an hon. member a memorandum with reference to the public building site there. We might clear that up.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext: Let that stand.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PROC EDURE RESUMING ON THURSDAY OR FRIDAY DEBATE ON AMENDMENT
speechtext:
Very well; I do not want to insist. The same applies to St. Stephen. The hon. member is here who asked for information as to why a contract was not let.
Progress reported.
